findings.reason: §2 would be re-scoped to trace, and choose between, `_local_fallback`'s `named_route` guard and `_review_lane_plan`'s skip, instead of hiring a worker to find a place that already exists and to build a fourth.
findings.text: §1's premise, "nothing in the system would have" moved the held review, is false, and §2's brief is scoped by that premise. The mechanism exists and refused on a one-line guard: `_local_fallback` (`reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:628`) rebinds a picker route to local when its metered lane stops serving, and returns `None` early at `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:637` when `pointer.get("named_route")` is set, which is exactly what the review carried (`{"backend": "codex", "set_by": "dispatch"}`, written at `reckon/crew/dispatch.py:1770`). The census of every existing "a held lane yields to the local lane" implementation, none named in §2 — (1) `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:628` `_local_fallback`, admission-time, guarded by `named_route`; (2) `reckon/crew/queue_admission.py:368`, the `replay_pick` condition inside `_launch_queued` (`:317`), a second `named_route` gate on the same launch path — it refuses the picker replay when `named_route` is set, so a repair that relaxes `_local_fallback` and not this one rebinds the lane and then refuses to re-pick on it; (3) `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:267` `continue_hold_on_its_offered_local_lane` with `_offered_local_backend` at `reckon/crew/dispatch_plan.py:243`, which already implements "a hold whose offered candidates include the local lane continues the request there", for picker holds; (4) `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1768` `_review_lane_plan` (via `_review_lane_candidates` at `:1813`), which already skips a lane and takes the next eligible candidate, on the lane's own published occupancy reading (`_current_lane_reading` at `:1718`, `_lane_over_ceiling` at `:1747`); (5) `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1438` `_failed_review_backend`, the dropped-lane demotion §1 cites as "as a lane that drops a review already does". Existing tests already pin these: `tests/test_route_before_queue.py:423` (named_route set_by dispatch) and `tests/test_a_review_waits_for_a_saturated_lane.py:184` (a saturated metered lane is passed over) — a repair that does not extend these files is a parallel mechanism

findings.reason: the finding names the file to extend and the third existing consumer (`budget_group.py:172`, `picker/snapshot.py:1621`) that reads the same review-lane rule, so a single-point repair lands where all three consumers see it rather than in a new review-only path.
findings.text: the brief's anchors route the worker to the wrong owner for the lane rule and name no owner at all for the hold. `_review_excluded_backends` (`reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1552`) and `_ordered_review_lanes` (`:1633`) are defined there; `reckon/crew/recovery.py:230` and `:242` are re-export shims, so §2's phrase "the review lane ordering in `reckon/crew/recovery.py`" names a pass-through. The budget-hold predicate's owner is likewise unnamed and has three pieces a new reader would fork: the hold verdict and its reason come from the pace policy in `reckon/budget.py` (burn and `resets_at` around `reckon/budget.py:1505` and `:1642`), the operator-facing wording is built by `_actionable_budget_hold` (`reckon/crew/dispatch_admission.py:77`), and the group/lift join a review ordering would need already exists inside the ordering itself — `_lifted_backends` at `reckon/crew/recovery_review_dispatch.py:1512` already calls `budget_group.declared_groups` and `budget_lift.published_readings`, which is the same wallet-to-lane map a hold check needs. So the honest owner to extend is `_ordered_review_lanes` / `_review_lane_plan`, reusing the existing lift join and the existing hold verdict, and the file the plan names is not it

rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan attributes the review lane ordering to `reckon/crew/recovery.py`, which only re-exports it, and leaves the budget-hold reader unnamed; both defects point a worker away from the owner it must extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 2360, cli_options 465, mcp_views 15, refusal_families 23; §2 adds no CLI option, public definition, MCP view or refusal family (it explicitly edits no product source and reuses the existing `awaiting-lane` / `held-by-gate` verdicts), so there is nothing for the section to retire or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §2's brief names `_ordered_review_lanes`, `_review_excluded_backends`, `caller_named_route` and "the admission budget hold", but omits the three mechanisms in this tree that already make a held lane yield (`_local_fallback`, `continue_hold_on_its_offered_local_lane`, `_review_lane_plan`), so the investigation is briefed to discover a place that already exists three times over.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the plan proposes no wrapper, and it does carry the anti-duplication requirement in its own text: the repair must read "the same budget check the admit pass uses" rather than re-deriving the hold.
